neighbours.label: The recipient pronoun right after 'told' (told you, told him, told them): the addressee of reported speech; the same pronoun after give or send should stay under it
fire: I told you the truth about the money last week.
As I told him, the contract ends in June.
Nothing I told them made any difference at all.
We already told you that the office is closed.
The doctor told her the results over the phone.
Everything he told you about me is a lie.
My brother told them where the keys were kept.
What I told you yesterday still holds today.
quiet: I gave you the money last week in cash.
As I paid him, the rain began in June.
Nothing I gave them made any difference at all.
We already sent you the form for the office.
The doctor gave her the results in an envelope.
Everything he gave you about me is in a box.
My brother showed them where the keys were kept.
What I paid you yesterday still holds today.

notes: Card: ' you' x6, ' me' x3, ' says' x2 in 'what we're telling you', 'Everything I told you', also Spanish señala 'ala', French nous dis-ons. Probe: told you 0.60-0.96, telling you 0.86, told them 0.49, told him 0.43; gave you 0.44 is a known risk, showing you 0.28, handed you 0.12, gave them 0.05. señala 0.96 and disons 0.98 fired but disent 0.05, so the Romance speech verbs are left out of this label.
